name: Alexander
overview: The name Alexander appears in several distinct contexts in Scripture, highlighting different individuals with varied roles. One Alexander is noted as the son of Simon of Cyrene, who was compelled to carry Jesus' cross (Mark 15:21), indicating a family connected to a significant moment in Christ's passion. Another Alexander, related to the high priest, was present during the defense of Peter and John in Jerusalem, showing involvement in early church conflicts (Acts 4:6). Additionally, a Jew named Alexander from Ephesus attempted to defend himself amid a public disturbance (Acts 19:33), while a different Alexander, identified as a coppersmith, opposed Paul and caused him harm (2 Timothy 4:14), illustrating opposition to the gospel. Finally, Paul references delivering an Alexander to Satan to correct blasphemy (1 Timothy 1:20), underscoring the seriousness of false teaching and its consequences.
